items.title: How a Skyrim Username Error Left an Innocent Man to Serve 18 Months in Jail
items.description: An innocent Canadian wrongly served 18 months in prison after Wisconsin police misspelled his Skyrim-inspired internet username.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
An innocent Canadian wrongly served 18 months in prison after Wisconsin police misspelled his Skyrim-inspired internet username.

Brandon Klayme from Halifax, Nova Scotia, was arrested in 2020 on charges of child luring and possession of child sex abuse imagery, after his username on chat app Kik was tracked down by U.S. cops.

But police made an error when identifying that Elder Scrolls IV: Skyrim username, Klayme's lawyers have now proven, finally securing their client's innocence six years later — and long after he served 18 months behind bars for crimes that someone else committed.

The case's 12-year-old victim identified the man talking to them on Kik as operating under the username "fus__ro_dah," a reference to Skyrim's infamous dragon language shout. Klayme, meanwhile, used the username "fus_ro_dah," a difference of one underscore.

In an affidavit submitted for his appeal seen by CBC News, Klayme said this difference had been "a subtle mistake that changed the course of my life."

"We noticed the problem when we were working on the appeal arguments this spring," Klayme's defence lawyer Zeb Brown told CBC News. "We were trying to figure out why the digital forensic evidence pointed at him given his denial of any involvement."

"If the correct username had been used at the start of the investigation, the subsequent steps in the investigation would not have led to Mr. Klayme," a subsequent appeal board declared. "In these circumstances, Mr. Klayme is factually innocent of the offences. He should never have been charged, let alone convicted."

As yet, there's no word where Klayme is pursuing any further claim after he was falsely imprisoned. For now, however, his name has been cleared.

Earlier this month, Skyrim publisher Bethesda announced that its beloved RPG had now officially crossed the 65 million units sold milestone, joining fellow fantasy role-playing game The Witcher 3 as one of the top 10 best-selling games of all time. Confirmation came from Bethesda boss Todd Howard, who outlined the company’s lineup of games following Xbox’s latest round of layoffs, with The Elder Scrolls 6 now a priority.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: The Elder Scrolls Online Content Delayed to 2027 Following Xbox Layoffs
items.description: The Elder Scrolls Online is undergoing some setbacks as a result of Xbox's recent reset and associated layoffs.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
The Elder Scrolls Online is undergoing some setbacks as a result of Xbox's recent reset and associated layoffs.

There has been a lot of speculation over the future of ESO for about a month now, and the team behind the game has stepped forward to clear the air. In a new blog post from game director Nick Giacomini, it is made clear that Elder Scrolls Online will continue and isn't on the verge of being shut down.

"Recently, we've been through a number of organizational changes and departures of teammates who helped shape The Elder Scrolls Online," he wrote. "We are profoundly grateful for everything they've contributed to the game and the community we've built together.

"At the same time, we've seen a lot of questions about what these changes mean for ESO. So let me be clear: ESO is here to stay, and our team is dedicated to the future of this game. Our focus hasn't changed. It is continuing to grow The Elder Scrolls Online and build upon the world millions of players call home."

Giacomini also outlined the team's plans to support the game going forward. He reaffirmed the recent news that ZeniMax Online Studios will be closely collaborating with Bethesda Game Studios on the future of The Elder Scrolls and stated that will give the team "new opportunities to share ideas" and create better experiences for players.

Unfortunately, the team is also delaying some content. Due to the recent restructuring at all Xbox-owned studios, the team has had to delay content in order to make sure it meets a level of quality that everyone can be satisfied with. So, the new Crimson Veldt trial, class and combat refreshes, and update 52 are all being pushed back to 2027.

"Instead of rushing to hit a previously announced deadline, we are giving our teams the runway they need to do things right," said the game director. "Some of our upcoming additions, like the Class and Combat Refresh and our new Trial, are highly complex, and we want to ensure they hit the mark before we put them in your hands."

There will still be plenty of content coming to Elder Scrolls Online in 2026, though. New stories, quests, and events are coming throughout the fall in addition to a new rumor system and quality of life upgrades. These pieces of content will roll out across September and October as part of Season 1 and Season 2.

As already noted, ZOS is also working closely with Bethesda Game Studio on the future of the IP. It's believed the studio will be assisting on the development of The Elder Scrolls 6, arguably the most important game that Xbox has on the horizon. The stakes are pretty high given the state of Xbox and the fact Starfield failed to meet expectations for many players. Bethesda will likely need all the help it can get to give something that justifies the long wait for this game.

Bethesda is also continuing to support its other big IP, Fallout. Remasters of Fallout 3 and New Vegas are in the works in addition to a new Fallout game from Obsidian Entertainment. Bethesda has also entered pre-production on Fallout 5, likely to ensure the team can make the jump to it after The Elder Scrolls 6 is finished.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Valve Says Steam Machine Reservations Will Be Filled By End of 2026
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
The Steam Machine has been out for about a month, but despite the eye-watering price, the console-PC hybrid has quite an extensive reservation list. And now Valve has come out with a blog post, saying anyone currently with a reservation list email will be able to buy the Steam Machine by the end of the year.

When the Steam Machine first came out, Valve put up a page allowing people to reserve the Steam Machine. Then, accounts were chosen at random and either placed on a reservation list or a waitlist. It's not clear how many people signed up for a Steam Machine, but it was apparently enough that it's going to take Valve the rest of the year to fulfill the orders.

It doesn't seem like every region has the same level of demand, though. Valve said in its blog that some people might move off of the waitlist and onto the reservation list depending on the region. In some regions, even, Valve has fulfilled its reservation list.

Valve told me in June that it expected to struggle to fulfill demand for the Steam Machine due to the ongoing RAM crisis. I don't know how much demand is there, but at least in my region, the Steam Machine is at the top of the Top Sellers list. Valve will probably never reveal exactly how many units it sells.

The company also took the opportunity to release the CAD files for the Steam Machine's exterior, so you can finally 3D print your own skins and face plates. Valve has also released FSR 4.1 support onto the experimental fork of Proton, for games that support FSR upgrade.

The Steam Machine has had a bit of a rocky launch. Not only did the RAM crisis – which is getting worse – force Valve to release the mini PC for a much higher price than it originally planned, but the company has had to reword its performance claims, too. It doesn't help that the Steam Machine is only about as powerful as the base PS5, but you can easily build a PC with SteamOS and better performance, if you don't mind a bigger machine.

Jackie Thomas is the Hardware and Buying Guides Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

items.title: Neon Genesis Evangelion Is Coming to Criterion Channel in September
items.description: Hideaki Anno’s legendary anime Neon Genesis Evangelion will officially stream on the Criterion Channel this September. Get the release details here.
items.author: Jim Vejvoda
items.content:
Neon Genesis Evangelion is coming to the Criterion Channel. IGN can exclusively reveal that director Hideaki Anno’s landmark anime series will debut on the Criterion Channel on September 1st.

“Set in a postapocalyptic world where teenagers pilot giant Multipurpose Humanoid Decisive Weapons–artificial humans known as Evangelions–to defend humanity from mysterious beings called Angels, the story evolves from high-stakes action spectacle into a deeply introspective exploration of identity, trauma, loneliness, and human connection,” as Criterion’s description of the boundary-pushing series reminds us.

The 1995-1996 series Neon Genesis Evangelion will be available on Criterion as will the feature films The End of Evangelion (1997) and Evangelion Death (True)² (1998).

All three titles come from North American distributor GKIDS.

The original twenty-six episode series will be available in both its Japanese-language version and the Classic English dub (the first time the latter will be available on streaming).

Other anime titles available on the Criterion Channel include Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex, The Garden of Words, and K-On! The Movie.

For more, read our look back at the evolution of the Neon Genesis Evangelion franchise, our picks for the Top 10 best sci-fi anime series of all time, and how to watch Evangelion in order.

Plus, find out about Makoto Shinkai’s Your Name returning to theaters in a new 4K remaster this August.

items.title: Of Course Jason Momoa's Blanka Does the Electrocution X-Ray Skeleton Attack in the Street Fighter Movie
items.description: We have a new look at the upcoming Street Fighter movie, this time showing off a decent chunk of a fight between Ryu and Blanka.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
We have a new look at the upcoming Street Fighter movie, this time showing off a decent chunk of a fight between Ryu and Blanka.

Ryu, played by Andrew Koji, finds himself in a cage and forced to fight by evil dictator, M. Bison. A chained Blanka, played by Jason Momoa, is dragged into the arena by hapless goons. And it doesn’t go very well for those goons — one is hit by Blanka’s electrocution power, and we see the x-ray skeleton visual effect that fans of the Street Fighter video games will know all too well.

The references to the fighting game franchise continue, as Blanka enters the fight with an immediate cannonball, as so many Blanka players start a match with. Blanka then tries a roundhouse kick followed by his iconic drop kick, which sends Ryu flying. Ryu pleads with Blanka, saying he doesn’t want to fight him. But Blanka isn’t having any of it, responding: “then, you die.”

Ryu then charges up a fireball, which explodes into the arena wall. It looks like it creates an opening through which I assume Ryu will make his escape.

This is our best look yet at Blanka in Street Fighter, and the VFX-drenched Momoa sounds while talking. Here, he’s got a sort of chirpy tone — he doesn’t appear to be a mindless beast, anyway. It will be interesting to see if Blanka gets much more screen time than this fight with Ryu, and, if so, his role in the overall story.

In the Street Fighter movie, Ken, played by Noah Centineo, and Ryu reconnect years after a falling out. Ryu has dropped off the radar in the ensuing years, growing long hair and a beard. Chun-Li, played by Callina Liang, is rounding up fighters for the world warrior tournament. She tells Ken, who had his own MTV show, that he's become a sideshow. In a lot of ways, Ken’s arc seems similar to Johnny Cage’s in the recently released Mortal Kombat 2 movie.

Street Fighter movie cast:

  • Noah Centineo as “Ken Masters”
  • Andrew Koji as “Ryu”
  • Callina Liang as “Chun-Li”
  • Joe “Roman Reigns” Anoai as “Akuma”
  • David Dastmalchian as “M. Bison”
  • Cody Rhodes as “Guile”
  • Andrew Schulz as “Dan Hibiki”
  • Vidyut Jammwal as “Dhalsim”
  • Eric André as “Don Sauvage”
  • Curtis ‘50 Cent’ Jackson as “Balrog”
  • Jason Momoa as “Blanka”
  • Orville Peck as “Vega”
  • Olivier Richters as “Zangief”
  • Hirooki Goto as “E. Honda”
  • Rayna Vallandingham as “Juli”
  • Alexander Volkanovski as “Joe”
  • Kyle Mooney as “Marvin”
  • Mel Jarnson as “Cammy”

And here's the official synopsis:

Set in 1993, estranged Street Fighters Ryu (Andrew Koji) and Ken Masters (Noah Centineo) are thrown back into combat when the mysterious Chun-Li (Callina Liang) recruits them for the next World Warrior Tournament: a brutal clash of fists, fate, and fury. But behind this battle royale lies a deadly conspiracy that forces them to face off against each other and the demons of their past. And if they don’t, it’s GAME OVER!

Street Fighter is set to hit theaters on October 16, 2026.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

items.title: After Pathfinder and One of the Best Warhammer 40,000 Games Ever Made, Owlcat's Next Step Is to Top Them All — and It's Grown to 600 People to Do It
items.description: After Pathfinder and one of the best Warhammer 40,000 games ever made, Owlcat's next step is to top them all — and it's grown to 600 people to do it.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Owlcat began life as a small developer, as so many do, but with plenty of expertise on the team. 2018's Pathfinder: Kingmaker, its first game, was successful, so the natural thing to do next was to make a bigger and better sequel. Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous followed in 2021. Another Pathfinder might have followed, but Owlcat took a significant step forward with 2023’s Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader, a sort of Baldur’s Gate 3 set in the Warhammer 40,000 universe game, rougher around the edges than Larian’s masterpiece, but no less meaty and with just as good writing. It’s a fantastic role-playing game, with plenty of choice and consequence. Many feel it’s one of the best Warhammer 40,000 video games ever made. It might even be the best.

Now, Owlcat has two announced games in production: Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy and The Expanse: Osiris Reborn. Dark Heresy continues Owlcat's impressive run of cRPGs, but The Expanse is something of a departure for the studio, a third-person action RPG made in the Mass Effect style. And so, what started as 15 people working together on Pathfinder is now a whopping 600-person development studio making multiple big projects. Owlcat has grown enormously in just a decade, and with that growth has come significant change to the way it develops games. But, co-founder and creative director Alexander Mishulin tells me, the studio has lost none of its passion for making RPGs that pack a real punch.

I’m a huge Warhammer 40,000 fan, as anyone who’s followed my articles on IGN over the last few years will probably know. For me, Rogue Trader put Owlcat on the map, and I assume opened doors for the company. Mishulin admits Rogue Trader was an important milestone, but he points to Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous as the real inflection point.

“It's a huge game with a lot of different choices and, even now, it comes up in a lot of top 10 games you don’t know about but you don’t want to miss,” Mishulin says. “We couldn’t make it without Kingmaker because it was our foundation to make a second game. But also, it showed a lot of people that we were serious about making great RPGs. When a studio does a second game and it is still successful, it is proof you can make these experiences over and over with new things, new ambition, new goals. It helped start a lot of discussions with different parties about what we can do next. And of course it helped establish a good relationship with Games Workshop while doing Rogue Trader.”

Owlcat pitched Rogue Trader before Wrath of the Righteous was even released, showing Games Workshop internal versions of Pathfinder to prove it was serious about making a great isometric RPG for Warhammer 40,000 fans. But yes, after Rogue Trader came out and was a success, more doors opened for discussions, both with publishers and IP holders about what the studio might do next.

Similarly, The Expanse was discussed while Rogue Trader was in the works — Owlcat showed The Expanse rights holder Alcon Entertainment first concepts during preliminary discussions during the final stages of Rogue Trader’s development. The Expanse, with its over the shoulder camera perspective and cinematic, action RPG gameplay, is clearly a departure for Owlcat, whose previous games had a top down isometric camera perspective and deep RPG mechanics. Dark Heresy follows the cRPG trend, although the twist here is there is a focus on an investigation system and the fantasy of being an Inquisitor (Warhammer 40,000’s Imperial detectives). Owlcat has other projects in the works, and these are different again (Mishulin won’t say what they are, as you’d expect).

What is success for Owlcat? The studio has three plans for its games before they come out. One, a plan for the minimal estimation of sales and revenue. Two, a plan for the average estimation, or what the game is supposed to achieve. And three, a plan for if a game sells very, very well, like in unexpected, viral hit terms. Rogue Trader performed “better than average,” Mishulin says, more successful, certainly, than Wrath of the Righteous, and more visible, but it wasn't a viral hit in the way Baldur's Gate 3 was.

Rogue Trader's success was, first and foremost, the result of it being a great game. But the comparison to Baldur’s Gate 3 (both games came out in the same year) actually helped Rogue Trader out, too — something Mishulin is very grateful for.

“We were really humbled that a lot of players and a lot of streamers compared us to BG3,” he says, “because BG3 is an enormous behemoth. It is one of the greatest RPGs ever made with a lot of ambition, passion, everything. We hope that at some point we will be able to compete directly, but not at the time of Rogue Trader. It is not like a real competition.

“On the other hand, BG3 did a great favor to a lot of RPG games. It brought them into the spotlight. Now RPGs can be a mainstream experience. When so many players enjoyed BG3, they started to look for what our next game will be, and we enjoyed this experience. ‘What can we try?’ Some of them go to our games to try them and enjoy them. So we are really grateful to Larian that they made such a great game not only because we enjoyed it — like, most of our developers played it for hundreds of hours — but also because they really made a lot of players aware of the genres and of the great games that are present there. Not only ours, but all of the games that are in there.”

Warhammer 40,000 as a setting, as a franchise, as a tabletop game, has never been bigger. I’ve spoken to plenty of video game developers who have told me now is the time to make a Warhammer 40,000 game, with huge interest in the IP. Saber Interactive’s Space Marine 2 took Warhammer 40,000 video games to a whole new level (its protagonist, Titus, is now one of the most prominent characters in the ongoing tabletop narrative). And assuming Henry Cavill’s Warhammer 40,000 Cinematic Universe actually gets off the ground, the franchise will only grow further.

Mishulin acknowledges that Owlcat has benefited from the enormous Warhammer 40,000 audience that found the fun in Rogue Trader. But he then flips this idea on its head, insisting Rogue Trader also brought people into the Warhammer 40,000 universe. “It probably will be a little bit arrogant, but I will still say it: I hope that our efforts also brought a little bit of this golden era for Games Workshop as well,” he quips.

items.title: EXCLUSIVE: How The Expanse: Osiris Reborn's Progression System Works, Plus Brand New Screenshots
items.description: The Expanse: Osiris Reborn is a third-person action RPG that has major Mass Effect vibes. But what’s different with this game is that your gear, not your class, defines the way you fight — and we’ve got exclusive details and screenshots to tell you how it all works.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
The Expanse: Osiris Reborn is a third-person action RPG that has major Mass Effect vibes. But what’s different with this game is that your gear, not your class, defines the way you fight — and we’ve got exclusive details and screenshots to tell you how it all works.

In Osiris Reborn, your origin shapes your captain's journey and mechanically defines where you find yourself starting, but it doesn’t define how you have to play. That is to say, character creation does not lock you into an RPG class. So, instead of choosing a fixed role, you develop your captain across four skill trees, but the weapons and gadgets you equip and upgrade ultimately define how you fight.

At the start of the game, you pick a specialization that sets your captain's initial skills and gear. For example, a cyber warfare specialist starts the game with decent gadget expertise, and their playstyle leans toward using abilities more than firearms. A firearms specialist, meanwhile, starts with better shooting and leadership skills, relying both on their own aim and on issuing orders to companions in combat.

But specializations do not restrict your progression or lock you into a particular role. For example, you can begin as a cyber warfare specialist, invest in weapon skills as you level up, and gradually turn your captain into a hybrid of a cyber warfare and firearms specialist. All four combat skill trees — Marksmanship, Gadgets, Survivalist, and Leader — remain open, so you are free to combine them and develop your captain in the direction that suits you.

The Expanse: Osiris Reborn combat skill trees

  • The marksmanship skill tree focuses on your mastery of various weapons and unlocks bonuses to critical damage, accuracy, and other combat modifiers.
  • The gadgets skill tree focuses on making your gadget-related abilities more powerful, increasing damage and duration, reducing the cooldown of abilities, etc.
  • The survivalist skills ensure your survival in combat by increasing your health, armor, armor regeneration capabilities, as well as providing unique bonuses that make you more lethal to your enemies while you are exposed or engage in melee.
  • The leader skill tree represents your ability to work with your crew. It provides various bonuses to your companions, such as weapon and ability damage, increased armor and damage reduction, and buffs for your own captain while companions are nearby.

While you can mix and match as you like, you can’t take everything. But you could lean into two directions at once. If you change your mind you can respec on your ship for a price (increases each time). This means you can't change your whole approach in the heat of battle, so you'll have to choose respecs carefully.

Gear then helps define your combat playstyle, and you can upgrade weapons and gadgets via the workbench. Every weapon and gadget you find can be upgraded at the workbench, shaping your abilities, your combat rhythm, and the way your captain fights.

Some upgrades are straightforward stat boosts: more damage, a wider radius, a shorter cooldown. Others are triggered effects, like a damage bonus that stacks with every kill. And a few rarer upgrades can unlock entirely new abilities for your gear.

Even gadgets like a simple frag grenade are upgradable, from a simple radius increase to emitting three extra projectiles that will explode and deal extra damage when you shoot them.

At each tier, you'll make an exclusive choice between two or three upgrade paths, pushing your gear toward your desired playstyle, until reaching the final tier, where the item can be upgraded with a powerful final perk. How far you can take an item depends on its quality. While you can't upgrade quality directly, you can find a higher-quality variation of the same weapon or gadget, which allows you to unlock further upgrade depth the original item lacked. Helpfully, you can reset gear upgrades, so you don’t lose the resources you invested in one item when you replace it with something better. A limited consumable lets you recover the upgrade resources, ensuring nothing is set in stone.

The image below shows the Kovach M46 rifle before and after a couple of upgrades. There's a bigger magazine, harder-hitting headshots, five-round bursts instead of three, and a scope for increased range.

Your companions have skill trees and signature gadgets with their own unique upgrade paths, too. Take Zafar, for example, an engineer who joins your team early in the game. With no upgrades, he installs a portable turret to hold a position. From there, you can substantially boost its rate of fire and enhance its targeting systems until it can actively intercept incoming enemy projectiles. Or, you can equip a heavy-caliber module to maximize its raw power, allowing it to deal heavy area-of-effect damage. Every companion you recruit brings their own gear, which you can customize to synergize with your playstyle.

Developer Owlcat says that it didn’t want to lock players into a fixed way of playing The Expanse: Osiris Reborn. “Instead of fixed classes, you are free to experiment with different playstyles until you find what you enjoy the most,” the studio said. “Your captain's arsenal and your companions’ skills and equipment are designed to adapt to your chosen playstyle.”

We’ve got much more on Owlcat, including an in-depth interview about the developer’s impressive journey from Pathfinder to Warhammer 40,000 and now The Expanse, as well as the studio’s response to calls from fans for it to make Baldur’s Gate 4.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

items.title: 'We Are a Little Bit Masochistic' — Developers Are Running Scared of Baldur's Gate 4, but Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader Studio Owlcat Would Consider It a 'Great Challenge'
items.description: Baldur’s Gate 4 appears to have developers running scared because they’re worried about meeting expectations set by Larian’s Baldur’s Gate 3. But one developer has said they would consider making the game a “great challenge” — although they’d avoid simply replicating what had gone before.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Baldur’s Gate 4 appears to have developers running scared because they’re worried about meeting expectations set by Larian’s Baldur’s Gate 3. But one developer has said they would consider making the game a “great challenge” — although they’d avoid simply replicating what had gone before.

After Larian decided against making Baldur’s Gate 4 and left Dungeons & Dragons behind to work on Divinity, fans have wondered which studio might be capable of taking on perhaps the toughest sequel in all video games. Among the studios that are often mentioned in online debates about who to turn to is Owlcat Games.

Owlcat is the developer of a number of well-received role-playing games including cRPG Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader, which was compared to Baldur’s Gate 3 upon its 2023 release. Rogue Trader is considered one of the best Warhammer 40,000 video games ever made, with fantastic characters, a gripping story, and over 100 hours of content — just like Baldur’s Gate 3.

While it didn’t quite reach the heights of Baldur’s Gate 3, Rogue Trader did well enough for Owlcat to secure a follow-up, Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy, which has many fans not just of Games Workshop’s grimdark setting on high alert, but cRPG fans rubbing their hands in anticipation.

So, would Owlcat answer the call, if Hasbro were to pick up the phone and ask it to make Baldur’s Gate 4? That’s the question I put to co-founder and creative director Alexander Mishulin, and… well, he didn’t say no!

“First of all, I would like to thank all the players, all your audience that consider us to be able to do that,” he began, diplomatically. “It's a really great honor. You already said that we are a little bit masochistic. So yeah, we will consider it a great challenge!”

Indeed I had said Owlcat was masochistic — for taking on the challenge of making Warhammer 40,000 games and a The Expanse game (we’ve got an exclusive reveal on The Expanse right here), as part of a wide-ranging interview in which we discuss Owlcat's enormous growth over the last decade. The Warhammer 40,000 and The Expanse universes each has a hardcore fanbase that puts any adaptation under intense scrutiny, but Owlcat is very much up for meeting player expectations, which is why Baldur’s Gate 4 might be a great fit.

It's worth noting that Mishulin is not confirming anything here, but understands what taking on Baldur's Gate 4 would involve, and the challenge Owlcat would face were matching the standards set by its predecessor. But, he suggests, that’s fine, because any developer simply trying to replicate a Larian game would be doomed to fail.

“In my opinion, Larian has made their own vision of how a sequel to Baldurs's Gate should be, and they presented it to us. “But other studios will do something differently. They will have their own DNA, their own ideas, and they will pour them into Baldur’s Gate 4, and it will be something else. I hope that there will be a studio brave enough and passionate enough and skillful enough to do that game.”

That long-running process and the invaluable feedback that came from it helped shape the game. But on top of that, the developers at Larian are just amazing at what they do, their writers are the best in the business, their quest designers the envy of the video game industry. Baldur’s Gate 3 is a masterpiece but it is also truly unique, with more content than any single player could ever hope to see. Most developers are not in the position to make a game like Baldur’s Gate 3. None, other than perhaps Rockstar, has the time, resources, or the freedom to make the sort of creative decisions that went into Baldur's Gate 3. Baldur’s Gate 3 is a single-player role-playing game that could last you forever, and truly, there are none in the modern era quite like it.

How do you follow Baldur’s Gate 3, then? Ohlen, clearly, couldn’t see a path forward. He said he’d need to start from scratch, because Larian has walked away from Dungeons & Dragons and taken its engine with it. So, he’d need at least half a decade to build the tech, and there’s no way Larian would agree to licensing out its engine.

Then there’s Larian boss Swen Vincke to contend with. He’s the CEO of the company and the majority shareholder, but he’s also the director of Baldur’s Gate 3, which means he is free to make creative decisions — for better and for worse. Most triple-A studio CEOs do not have such freedom or control.

"Swen's always going to be the master of building those kinds of things,” Ohlen said. “It's really hard to take him off that throne, just because of everything — the tools, institutional knowledge, team."

items.title: Helldivers 2 x Warhammer 40,000 Castellan's Creed Legendary Warbond Fully Revealed, Weapons and Armor Shown Off, Release Date Confirmed
items.description: As promised, we have the full reveal of the Helldivers 2 x Warhammer 40,000 Legendary Warbond today, a first look at the weapons and armor it will include, and a release date.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
As promised, we have the full reveal of the Helldivers 2 x Warhammer 40,000 Legendary Warbond today, a first look at the weapons and armor it will include, and a release date.

“Roll the dice to break the traitorous enemies of Super Earth in this historic crossover Legendary Warbond,” developer Arrowhead said. “Fight for Liberty without measuring distance, line-of-sight or your target’s chances of survival with potent weapons, formidable armor, and so much more.”

In a post on Steam, Arrowhead said the Warbond is inspired by the Astra Militarum (formely known as the Imperial Guard) regiment, the Cadian Kasrkin, which most fans had predicted.

“This deployment of advanced firearms, armor, patterns and more, has been recreated in honor of the valiant Helldivers who gave their lives in a heroic last stand to defend the peaceful world of Chara during the First Galactic War,” Arrowhead continued, referencing Warhammer 40,000 planet, Cadia. Cadia is one of the most famous worlds in the Warhammer 40,000 setting, and its people some of the toughest in the Emperor’s human army. Cadia is no more (that’s a whole thing all its own), but its people live on, as do their wargear.

“Now you have the opportunity to unleash a devastating new type of Freedom on the battlefield in their eternal memory," Arrowhead continued. “Dive in. Deploy out. Spread Managed Democracy all about.”

You can see all the items in the slideshow of images, below.

The warbond includes the R/40-K Hot-Shot Marksman Rifle

Primary - This weapon is a testament to Charan craftsmanship, deadly at close range, deadlier at long range. Engineered for precision on the battlefield, every shot fired is a declaration of intent. This will make a worthy addition to any Helldiver's arsenal.

The P/40-K Bolt Pistol (this was teased last week)

Sidearm - A sidearm which has withstood the test of time. Known for its versatility and raw stopping power, it causes even the most hardened enemies to quiver in its presence. Never leave your Super Destroyer without one.

The 40-K Meltagun stratagem

Stratagem- Firing a short-ranged, superheated beam of thermal energy capable of reducing steel to slag. Effective at melting away any traces of undemocratic values from even the toughest of foes.

And the G/40-K Meltamine

Throwable - A proximity activated burst mine that is dangerous to friend and foe alike, said to burn brighter than the sun itself. Place wisely, Helldiver. Mind your step.

Armor wise, we have the TG-8 Sharpshooter

Medium Armor - For the soldier who does what needs to be done, no matter the cost. The TG-8 is not armor for survival, it is armor for obedience. Spread Managed Democracy at any cost.

Armor Passive - True Grit

+20 weapon handling, +30% reload speed for support weapons

And the TG-122 Demo-Trooper

Heavy Armor - The Ministry of Defense has faithfully recreated this storied Charan armor for a new wave of Helldivers. Built to endure the harshest warzones known to mankind. Wear the history, carry on the legacy, and champion Freedom.

Armor Passive - True Grit

+20 weapon handling, +30% reload speed for support weapons

Other items include

  • Cape/Player Card: Camo Cloak
  • Cape/Player Card: City Fighter's Resolve
  • Title: Still Standing
  • Pattern: Castellan’s Green

The Helldivers 2 x Warhammer 40,000 Castellan’s Creed Legendary Warbond launched August 12. It’s worth noting that you will not be able to claim the warbond with a Premium Warbond token.

Even before the Warhammer 40,000 crossover was announced, fans had spoken about how it would be the perfect fit for Helldivers 2, which sees groups of four soldiers essentially play the role of cannon fodder in the endless galactic war against horrible alien monsters. You can quite easily equate Helldivers’ alien bug race, the Terminids, to Warhammer 40,000’s Tyranids, for example. The Automatons aren’t a million miles away from the mindless mechanical Necrons, either.

Warhammer 40,000 is something Arrowhead was often asked about in interviews, and by that I mean that I had asked the team about it in interviews because I love this stuff. In April last year, I asked Alex Bolle, production director on Helldivers 2, about a potential Warhammer 40,000 collab, and he said discussions were being had. "Obviously Warhammer 40,000 is something that a lot of guys internally love to death," he said at the time. "So the devs are discussing, the devs are proposing stuff, and the hype is building. So these are discussions internally that we are having. Warhammer 40,000, I can't really tell you. Maybe. Who knows? We'll see!"

Indeed, in 2024, Arrowhead's Johan Pilestedt published an extended list of IPs he “really would love to do a take on," and Warhammer 40,000 was right up there alongside the likes of Aliens, Starship Troopers, and Terminator.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

items.title: Long-Lost Pokémon Game Apparently Pops Up on eBay After 20 Years — Though You'll Need $9,000 to Buy It
items.description: A long-lost Pokémon game briefly available in Japan 20 years ago appears to have popped up on eBay, priced at around $9,000.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
A long-lost Pokémon game briefly available in Japan 20 years ago appears to have popped up on eBay, priced at around $9,000.

Pokémon Fishing Contest DS was only playable at special events and from Pokémon Center locations in Japan for a few months back in 2005, as part of a high score contest.

Like other Nintendo DS Download Play titles, the game was received via Wi-Fi and only lasted on your own handheld until you powered it down. Oh, and you could only download it at participating venues from May to August 2005.

With no way to save the experience, the software was subsequently thought lost — until now, as what looks to be a Nintendo DS test cartridge holding files for the game is up for sale — priced €7,999 (around $9,145).

ポケパーク釣り大会のソフトがebayに出てる！https://t.co/4MtM4R0lZA

2005年頃にイベントで配信されたソフト。https://t.co/p1SiRR8NyS pic.twitter.com/YfJKkrZdoW

— ティラミス (@Tiramisu090401) July 28, 2026

While the pictured cartridge appears bulky, this is indeed a Nintendo DS test cartridge, whose upper part protrudes from the console. These devices were typically never seen in public, and instead reserved for Nintendo and third-party DS game developers to test work-in-progress software builds. Rarely, these cartridges were sent out to media to preview in-development games, though would need to be returned after.

It's unclear where this particular cartridge has originated. The eBay listing appears to come from a German seller who has previously focused on selling Pokémon plushies. There are also questions over whether this test cartridge contains a playable version of Pokémon Fishing Contest DS, or server code meant to collect its high scores from players.

Long considered lost media, the software for the Poképark Fishing Tournament has become available for sale…
Hopefully it will fall into the hands of someone who wishes to preserve it so everyone else can experience it once more.
Fingers crossed that some hoarder doesn’t buy it… https://t.co/hCluPlfAqs pic.twitter.com/88dw2JiWpx

— Professor Rex🇨🇦 (@RexProfessor) July 29, 2026

"This listing is for the exact physical development/test cartridge shown in the photos," the seller states. "Acquired as part of a private lot, no further history or provenance documentation is available. It's in working condition and when tested on a retail Nintendo DS, it boots to a Japanese-language screen indicating a high-score ranking communication program. DSi and 3DS compatibility is not confirmed. No additional functionality has been tested or is guaranteed. Sold strictly as a physical item as-is."

Responding to the sale on social media, several fans have suggested that the cartridge should be bought by someone willing to share its contents with the wider Pokémon community as a matter of game preservation. Alas, at the time of writing, the eBay listing is currently yet to attract any bids.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey Sparks Assassin's Creed: Odyssey Player Count Spike, Gives Ubisoft 'Great Ammunition' for a Remake
items.description: Ubisoft's excellent Assassin's Creed Odyssey is enjoying a big spike in active players, following the launch of Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Ubisoft's excellent Assassin's Creed Odyssey is enjoying a big spike in active players, following the launch of Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey.

Nolan's Ancient Greek blockbuster is on track to make a billion dollars at the box office, and has clearly sparked further interest in its setting. Indeed, engagement statistics published by Alinea Analytics analyst Rhys Elliot show that the film's launch has also driven thousands of players back to Ubisoft's 2018 epic.

Assassin's Creed Odyssey has nearly doubled its active userbase over the past week across a combination of PlayStation, Xbox and PC via Steam. Xbox engagement was particularly strong, up from 36,000 to 84,000 daily active users, a leap of 134%.

In what seems to be a canny move, Ubisoft currently has Assassin's Creed Odyssey available via Xbox Game Pass and PlayStation Plus — allowing The Odyssey fans who own a console subscription to boot up the game without any additional charge.

"Software sales moved modestly at around 400,000 copies year-to-date, but the real [benefit] here is pure player engagement," Elliot wrote, going on to suggest the figures bode well for a future Odyssey remake akin to the recently-launched Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced.

"The film didn't make millions buy an eight-year-old game, but it got a massive cohort playing it again," Elliot continued. "That data gives Ubisoft great ammunition for an eventual AC Odyssey Resynced.

"Credit to Ubisoft for leaning into the momentum. They ran timed social campaigns alongside Nolan’s release and resurfaced Discovery Tour (the guided, combat-free educational mode), positioning it as an interactive companion piece for anyone falling down a history rabbit hole after leaving the cinema."

Ancient Greece awaits, misthios.
Time to begin an Odyssey (again). pic.twitter.com/VKFlTOJrVq

— Assassin's Creed (@assassinscreed) July 15, 2026

Assassin's Creed Odyssey is an epic, standout entry in Ubisoft's long-lived historical adventure series, and one that's well worth experiencing (or revisiting, if you played it back in the day). It features an enormous world to explore, filled with a sprawling set of stories taking in the setting's historical characters, myths and legends. Odyssey also saw the series leaning its furthest into full RPG territory, to the delight of many (though the chagrin of others who preferred the franchise in its more humbler rooftop-set origins).

With more than 10 million copies sold during its first two years, Odyssey remains one of the most successful entries in the Assassin's Creed series, while its protagonist Kassandra continues to be one of its most popular, and one of the few to pop up again in subsequent games.

Just don't expect the events of either The Odyssey or Assassin's Creed Odyssey to overlap. While some elements will be familiar, the former is set around 800 years before — although it clearly inspired Ubisoft's game. Both stories follow an outcast navigating the Greek islands on a ship, battling armies and other monstrous forces as they attempt to reclaim their family. Not played Assassin's Creed Odyssey yet? Now's the time.

While some elements will be familiar, the former is set around 800 years before — although it clearly inspired Ubisoft's game. Now's the time.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Quest The Hunt, With Its Creepy Cartoon and Disturbing Braindance, Was Meant to Feel Like True Detective
items.description: Cyberpunk 2077 is nearly six years old, but fans are still reminiscing about some of its best parts, and its developers are still revealing fresh insights into its creation.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Cyberpunk 2077 is nearly six years old, but fans are still reminiscing about some of its best parts, and its developers are still revealing fresh insights into its creation.

Warning! Spoilers for Cyberpunk 2077 follow…

The Hunt is a side quest where you join forces with River Ward to investigate a serial killer called Anthony Harris, who River believes has kidnapped his nephew, Randy. Fans have praised The Hunt for how it reveals the serial killer, who at the start of the quest is in a coma in hospital having been apprehended by police.

The player picks up snippets of insight into Harris’ character as they search for clues as to Randy's whereabouts. You learn how Harris grew up and delve deep into his psychology through detective work, with little to no combat involved.

During a search of Randy's room, V and River log onto his computer to view his activity on the net. At this point you discover Harris and Randy were exchanging messages, and there’s a, well, a very creepy cartoon saved onto his computer.

This cartoon is used to unlock Harris’ mind for a braindance and, well, it's pretty messed up in there. After learning more about what makes Harris tick, you eventually track down where he was keeping his victims and rescue Randy before it’s too late. It turns out Harris was "farming" teenage boys, like the cow depicted in the cartoon, to try to "fix" them. For Harris, that meant pumping them full of drugs.

Responding to praise for The Hunt on social media, Paweł Sasko, associate game director on Cyberpunk 2, explained what CD Projekt was going for with the quest.

“The Hunt quest is a psychological thriller, violence is almost never shown on the screen, its delivery is through deliberate and quite low key narrative tools, such as files, emails, while the major discovery is hidden inside a BD. Shocking revelation comes as a result of performing authentic police work, intentionally not an action sequence.”

“It was meant to feel like True Detective, cop drama in cyberpunk setting, entangled with the storyline of River Ward,” Sasko continued. “Creepy cartoon points towards the abuse villain experienced as a child, every slap feels uncomfortable and wrong, discovering cow in feeders makes the skin crawl.

“That’s what I love about cyberpunk setting: we can juggle genres and themes to spice things up, surprise and delight the player.”

Cyberpunk 2077 is full of quests like this (the Sinnerman and They Won't Go When I Go side jobs spring to mind), where the game doubles down on disturbing elements. You’d imagine Cyberpunk 2 will have more of the same, too.

Speaking of which, Cyberpunk 2 had 163 people working on it of the end of April. While we know little about it, Cyberpunk creator Mike Pondsmith teased some details when he was asked about the scope of his involvement with what was then known as Project Orion, back at the Digital Dragons 2025 conference. It sounds like we'll have to wait some time to find out more. CD Projekt is of course focusing on The Witcher 4, and CD Projekt has suggested Cyberpunk 2 won’t be out until at least 2030.

items.title: In a Bid for New Viewers, The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 Begins With a Fellowship-Style Prologue
items.description: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power will begin its third season with a Fellowship of the Ring-style prologue, designed to explain the series' status quo to new or lapsed viewers.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power will begin its third season with a Fellowship of the Ring-style prologue, designed to explain the series' status quo to new or lapsed viewers.

The Rings of Power Season 3 feels like something of a reset for Amazon's mega-expensive but divisive Middle-earth show. A five-year time jump is moving the series' narrative forward, key characters such as Gandalf and Sauron are now fully revealed and clearly the focus, while the less-popular Harfoots have been sidelined.

A prologue-style catch-up makes sense, then, to ease audiences into the series, which is now approaching its mid-point of five planned seasons. And even for loyal returning viewers, it has still been two years since Rings of Power's last episode. With so much to explain about the state of Middle-earth after two seasons of build-up, a voiceover akin to Galadriel's at the start of Fellowship makes sense to set the stage for what's to come.

Speaking to Empire magazine, showrunners J. D. Payne and Patrick McKay said the time-jump into the middle of Sauron's war on Middle-earth and accompanying prologue catch-up were deliberate tactics to get as many viewers as possible on board.

"It was a calculated decision to start with real momentum, and hopefully bring a few more people onto the train," McKay said.

"The first two seasons were all about building out this world," he continued, painting the show's freshman and junior years as their own prologue to what happens next. "Throughout that time, we're lighting all these fuses and setting all these stories in motion. The third season is when all those bombs are starting to explode."

For more casual Lord of the Rings viewers, Season 3 will include numerous familiar elements from Peter Jackson's film trilogy, such as the One Ring (which is finally created by Sauron), the Ringwraiths (or an early version of them), plus more from the Balrog (which now talks for some reason). Its focus seems to squarely be on Sauron's antics as his armies swarm Middle-earth, and the attempts by the Elves to repel him.

Meanwhile, Gandalf is busy with the Dark Wizard from the East, whose identity will also be revealed this season (fans believe he is likely one of the two Blue Wizards left out of Tolkien's main work). The dull political plotline of Númenor will also return, though is not being talked up as a main focus.

Here's the official blurb on The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power:

In Season 3, Middle-earth is at war. Five years have passed since the fall of Eregion. Sauron’s armies have marched across the whole of the world, conquering all in their path. Only a few isolated pockets stand between the Dark Lord and total victory — Khazad-dûm, where the Dwarves are now sealed deep within their mountain halls, and the elven realms of Lindon and Rivendell, which are protected by their Three Rings. But deep in the land of Mordor, in his newly completed tower of Barad-dûr, the Dark Lord toils day and night, obsessed with harnessing a power that will bring the last of his enemies to their knees: One Ring to rule them all... Now, all the free peoples of Middle-earth — Dwarves, Elves, Men, and Wizards alike — must find a way to come together, in a race against time to prevent Sauron from achieving his goal of utter domination of all life…

The first four episodes of Season 3 of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power premiere on November 11, 2026. Episodes five and six will be available to stream on November 18, and the final two episodes of the season will be released on November 25.

Amazon says The Rings of Power is one of the highest performing and most-viewed titles ever on Prime Video. Season 1 is the biggest TV series premiere in the history of Prime Video, and Season 2 is among the Top 5 most-watched returning seasons ever. The series has attracted over 185 million viewers worldwide so far.

Image credit: Samir Hussein/WireImage via Getty Images.

items.title: The Divisive Harfoots Take a 'Backseat' in The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3
items.description: Don’t expect to see the Harfoots in The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3. They’re taking a “backseat,” co-showrunner J.D. Payne has said.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Don’t expect to see the Harfoots in The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3. They’re taking a “backseat,” co-showrunner J.D. Payne has said.

Warning! Spoilers for The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power follow…

The Harfoots are one of the most divisive groups of people in Amazon’s The Lord of the Rings prequel series. They are an ancestral, nomadic branch of hobbits who lived hidden in Rhovanion during the Second Age, operating under a strict migratory lifestyle driven by the motto, "Nobody goes off-trail, and nobody walks alone."

In Season 1 of The Rings of Power, the Harfoots discover The Stranger (who later turns out to be Gandalf), and go on a journey together. In Season 2, Harfoots Nori Brandyfoot and Poppy Proudfellow travel to the arid lands of Rhûn, get separated from the Stranger, and encounter a settled village of early hobbit ancestors known as the Stoors. At the end of Season 2, the Harfoots say goodbye to Gandalf and join forces with the Stoors on a new migration.

Which leads us to Season 3. In an interview with Empire magazine, Payne confirmed the Harfoots absence. “It was time for them to take a little bit more of a backseat,” Payne said. “But I will also say: never count a Halfling out.”

Whether that means Nori will make a cameo appearance in Season 3, or the Harfoots return in future seasons is unclear. What is clear, though, is that we won’t see a main storyline featuring the Harfoots this time around, which is a significant change from the show so far.

Why the switch? It’s fair to say the Harfoots weren’t particularly well received by The Lord of the Rings fans. Apart from ongoing questions about deviating from J. R. R. Tolkien’s works (Tolkien did not place hobbits or Harfoots in active, major plots during the Second Age, but then he didn’t write much of anything about the Second Age), some felt they were annoying, their storyline frustratingly slow, and their Irish accents… a choice.

So, I doubt many will shed a tear over the Harfoots failing to turn up in Season 3. The focus this time around appears to be Sauron’s bid to forge the One Ring (and seeking the power to do so from a talking Balrog), the introduction of Galadriel's husband, Celeborn, and Gandalf becoming full-on Gandalf.

There doesn’t seem much room for the Stoors in Season 3, either, but Empire asked if Sméagol, who was a Stoor, might turn up in the form of a Gollum origin story at some point in the future. “We have lots of ideas for future seasons,” co-showrunner Patrick McKay replied. “Stay tuned, is all we’d say right now.”

The first four episodes of Season 3 of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power premiere on November 11, 2026. Episodes five and six will be available to stream on November 18, and the final two episodes of the season will be released on November 25.

Amazon says The Rings of Power is one of the highest performing and most-viewed titles ever on Prime Video. items.title: Project Motor Racing Adds Free Holden Commodore, PC Triple-Screen Support in 2.1 Update
items.description: New, free V8 Supercars DLC pack launches alongside a “significant new update” for Project Motor Racing, which includes a total rebuild of the handling model for the GT3 and GT4 categories.
items.author: Luke Reilly
items.content:
Giants Software and Straight4 Studios have launched a new, free DLC pack alongside a “significant new update” for Project Motor Racing. Update 2.1 includes a total rebuild of the handling model for the GT3 and GT4 categories, Alpha triple-screen support on PC, and more.

The ‘Aussie Rivals’ pack brings one of the greatest rivalries in motorsport to Project Motor Racing for the first time, introducing the 2013 Holden VF Commodore and a “completely reworked” 2013 Ford Falcon FG. These Australian domestic models represented the last truly local clash between Holden and Ford, before Holden transitioned to the imported ZB Commodore shell in 2018 and the death of car manufacturing in Australia saw the Supercars series subsequently shift to Chevrolet Camaro and Ford Mustang shells. This era of V8 Supercar racing has been represented in a string of Forza Motorsport games, as well as on iRacing and 2014’s Grid Autosport, but never in Gran Turismo – so this may come as particularly appetising for PS5 players.

Alongside the DLC pack comes Update 2.1, which – according to Straight4 – “delivers major improvements across content, physics, online racing, immersion, presentation, and close-quarters racing.”

The update includes a complete rebuild of the GT4 and GT3 classes led by new CCO Aristotelis Vasilakos, former handling guru at Kunos Simulazioni for Assetto Corsa. It also features Alpha triple-screen support, improved collisions, and various “graphical enrichments throughout the game.” Logitech’s ‘Trueforce’ feedback has also now been enabled on all platforms.

Players will now be able to join supported online sessions after they have started, without having to wait for the next full restart, and those registered for a ranked session will no longer need to stay on the registration screen while they wait. That is, once you’re registered you’ll be able to return to other areas of the game. When the ranked session is good to go, you’ll get a notification that will allow you to join directly from wherever you are.

“Players have been putting in the laps, giving us the feedback, and pushing us to make PMR better,” said new Straight4 Studios CEO Kevin Boland. “Update 2.1 is the result of that process: a major GT4 and GT3 overhaul, cleaner racing, better online flow, stronger immersion features, and the free Aussie Rivals Pack, delivered as a big thank you to our community that continues to inspire and shape Project Motor Racing.”

This new update follows an earlier major update for Project Motor Racing released back in March, which “aimed at resetting PMR’s foundation and bringing the sim much closer to what a serious motorsport title should feel like.”

items.title: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma Gives Optimistic Outlook Despite Grim Fiscal Earnings Report
items.description: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma responded to the company’s Q4 2026 fiscal report, which showed a continued decline in earnings for both content and hardware.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma responded to the company’s Q4 2026 fiscal report, which showed a continued decline in earnings for both content and hardware.

Microsoft’s Form 10-K SEC filing has been released, showing that Xbox has continued to experience notable revenue loss at the end of their 2026 fiscal year. As told in the filing, Xbox’s revenue decreased by $1.7 billion, or 7%, driven by declines in Xbox content, services, and Xbox hardware.

items.title: Battlefield 6's Record-Breaking Success Earns EA CEO $38 Million Payday, But Laid-Off Devs Aren't Around to Celebrate
items.description: EA’s CEO got an $8 million raise thanks to how well Battlefield 6 performed — four months after the devs responsible for making the game got laid off.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
EA’s CEO got an $8 million raise thanks to how well Battlefield 6 performed — four months after the devs responsible for making the game got laid off.

Battlefield 6 was the highest-selling game of 2025, beating out Call of Duty: Black Ops 7 and NBA 2K26. It sold over seven million copies in just three days and was the best-selling title across both Xbox and PC at the time.

However, in March 2026 — just five months after celebrating the most successful launch in the Battlefield franchise ever — EA laid off an undetermined number of employees across all its Battlefield teams to “better align” itself around “what matters most to our community.”

Now, come July, one of EA’s SEC filings have been released, showing that CEO Andrew Wilson’s total compensation for the 2026 fiscal year added up to $38,649,984.

As pointed out by PC Gamer, this is an $8 million increase from his total compensation from the previous year, and he has Battlefield 6’s success to thank for it.

The filing credits Battlefield 6’s high sales for allowing EA to meet company objectives, saying the game had a “high-quality launch” with “positive critical reviews and stable services and gameplay, with interim milestones related to future launches being met.” It also states that the game’s “highly successful launch” helped manage the company’s resilience in an “unpredictable external environment.”

While reception to Battlefield 6 has had its ups and downs in recent months, it’s showing no signs of slowing on the content side, receiving a collaboration with Top Gun as part of Season 4. The collab, which drops in August, includes two fighter jets and skins of characters in the film, complete with full voice acting.

In June, IGN spoke with Ariel Giovannetti, Seasonal and Competitive Creative Lead, Motive, Battlefield Studios, who assured fans that their feedback about the game is being heard and that the team was pleased with how things shook out in Season 3.

“I hope the roadmap shows that we are listening, that we are working towards those goals that the community is setting for us, but at the same time we're moving responsively because Battlefield is huge,” he told us.

“...our goal was to reach out to our fans, was to reach out to our current players, show them that we care, show them that the future is bright, that we are going to be applying a lot of changes, that we're going to be doing a lot of things, that is what the community wants and we're very happy with that.”

This news follows EA's 2025 aquisition to a private investor group in a record-breaking $55 billion deal, made up of Saudia Arabia's Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners, who now have a 100% ownership of the company.

items.title: Marvel Studios Boss Suggests Kingpin Appearing in a Spider-Man Movie Isn't as Complicated as Fans Think
items.description: Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige has given fans hope about the possibility of Kingpin showing up in a Spider-Man movie.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige has given fans hope about the possibility of Kingpin showing up in a Spider-Man movie.

For years, some of our favorite Marvel characters have been wrapped up in complicated rights issues. Although Disney owns the bulk of the Marvel universe, there are some characters who are tied up elsewhere. Spider-Man's film rights are still owned by Sony, but are essentially loaned out to Marvel Studios for new live-action films and crossover events. The Hulk's solo films belong to Universal Pictures, which is why there hasn't been a new Hulk movie since 2008. And Kingpin is also apparently in some kind of legal purgatory.

Wilson Fisk actor Vincent D'Onofrio has expressed interest in playing the character in a Spider-Man film or even in his own spin-off movie, but has said it's not possible. In 2025, he claimed his character is only permitted to show up in TV shows.

"It's a very hard thing to do, for Marvel to use my character," said the Daredevil: Born Again actor. "It's a very hard thing to do, because of ownership and stuff. I’m only usable for television shows. Not even a one-off Wilson Fisk movie. It’s all caught up in rights and stuff. I don’t know when that would work out — or if it ever would work out at all.”

However, Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige suggests it's not as big of a deal as people may think. When speaking with Josh Horowitz, Feige was asked whether or not Kingpin and Daredevil were ever considered for roles in Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Feige downplayed D'Onofrio's concern over rights issues and stated that the characters were actually considered

"There are things to navigate like everything else," said Feige. "We talked about all those characters at one point."

Ultimately, it sounds like Feige could get the job done if the story demanded it. Will that ever happen? Who's to say! It would be awesome to see Fisk and Spidey duke it out on the big screen, though. However, Feige has managed to not only usher in Spider-Man into the MCU despite rights issues, but he also managed to bring the X-Men, Fantastic Four, and Daredevil into the MCU after years of rights issues and different ownership. Maybe Feige will work his magic for New York's notorious crime boss one day.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Kevin Feige 'Has Hope' That Spider-Man and Venom Will Finally Meet in the MCU
items.description: Marvel President Kevin Feige has said he’s holding out hope that Spider-Man and Venom will one day have their long-awaited crossover in the MCU.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Marvel Studios President Kevin Feige has said he’s holding out hope that Spider-Man and Venom will one day have their long-awaited crossover in the MCU.

Speaking to Josh Horowitz on the Happy Sad Confused podcast, Feige and film producer Amy Pascal chatted about the possibility of seeing the two characters finally meet up in a Marvel movie. While they didn’t say anything definitively, their remarks hinted that it’s something Marvel Studios is keenly aware of, though how realistic it actually is remains up in the air.

Horowitz asked the pair if they could reveal “how close” they’ve gotten to putting Tom Hardy’s Venom in a flick with Tom Holland’s Spider-Man, remarking that it’s been a major “bummer” the two haven’t had a single moment together after all these years.

“It would be great, let’s put it that way,” Pascal said diplomatically.

“Do you have hope?” Horowitz said, prompting Feige to vaguely answer, “We always have hope.”

“I have hope. We have hope,” Pascal playfully interjected.

While this answer, ironically, doesn’t give fans much hope that we’ll see these two versions of the characters share the screen anytime soon, Feige and Pascal did confirm that an animated Venom movie is still in the works.

News of this film first broke on February 23, 2026. Zach Lipovsky and Adam B. Stein, the duo behind Final Destination: Bloodlines, are set to direct the full-length feature, with names like Amy Pascal and even Tom Hardy himself said to be involved, though the exact nature of their relationship to the project is still unknown.

Plot details are also scarce, leaving fans anxious to know what adventure the Symbiote will go on next. Most are hopeful it’ll at least be a better experience than Venom: The Last Dance, which IGN’s Tom Jorgensen gave a 4 out of 10, citing its “boring, generic plot and bad action” that left audiences equal parts snoozing and confused at the cinema.

This is the latest news we’ve heard about a Spider-Man and Symbiote crossover after Tom Holland discussed the situation in response to a young fan during an interview for Brand New Day. “One day, I’m sure we’ll get to see the symbiote,” he said, though he admitted he couldn’t directly say whether or not it appears in the film.

The newest Spidey movie hits theaters on Friday, July 31. IGN scored the flick a 7 out of 10, saying it “effectively refocuses on the sturdiest pillars of the webslinger's iconography: struggling to find balance while swinging around New York City saving the day, and looking dang cool doing it.”

items.title: 'It Totally Didn't Work' - Tom Holland and Zendaya 'Hated' an Early Cut of Spider-Man: Brand New Day
items.description: Tom Holland has revealed that he, Zendaya, and Jacob Batalon "hated" an early cut of Spider-Man: Brand New Day.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Tom Holland has revealed that he, Zendaya, and Jacob Batalon "hated" an early cut of Spider-Man: Brand New Day.

When speaking with Quotable, Tom Holland was asked about what it feels like to finish such a massive film. He noted that he doesn't feel complete until the film has been out for a while and audiences have had a chance to respond to it, partially because a movie changes a lot from script to production to post-production. He went on to speak about how they watched a bunch of different cuts of the Brand New Day as part of this process, and the starring trio outright hated one of them.

"We've seen loads of different cuts of this movie, and one of the cuts, they took all of the notes from all of the random people who saw the film," said Holland. "And then they changed the movie, and we watched it, and we hated it. It totally didn't work. It was what the people were asking for, but it wasn't quite what we wanted as the creatives. But they learned lessons from that experience, so a movie can change in a thousand different ways in the edit room."

What Holland is seemingly speaking about is feedback from test screenings. Films will often show rough cuts to random audiences to gain feedback, but this has its pros and cons. One random audience can't always accurately predict how everyone will feel. Sometimes movies have been unintentionally butchered by test audiences who didn't understand it. It's up to the creative team to more or less decipher the underlying feedback that can actually help strengthen the project, as opposed to just taking it all at face value.

Luckily, it sounds as though the Spider-Man team was able to sift through the noise and make something that aligned with their vision while taking advantage of feedback. Spider-Man: Brand New Day currently boasts a 91% rating on Rotten Tomatoes and is tracking to have the biggest opening weekend of 2026. We gave the movie a 7/10, noting that it covers familiar ground for Spidey, but still managed to be an enjoyable adventure.
